summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.37/1550)

data.turoyo: Nošo i naqqayo, awqaf, l nošo lə mraǧaʕwo.
data.translation: No one at that time—the endowments—no one appealed.

rationale: New II.1 Infectum-wa box; property/endowment application context without asserting a technical appellate procedure.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.39/1748)

data.turoyo: Maʕlum yo ya Ǧan i naqqayo rasmi latwoban mraǧʕinawo. Xəṣuṣi mraǧʕinawo, čəngi lə kowe tafriqa bi mamlake, d saymət tafriqa bi mamlake, tabəʕ d ǧazayo.
data.translation: Of course, Jan, at that time we could not make applications officially. We made applications privately, because there must be no discrimination in the country. If you make distinctions in the country, you are liable to punishment.

rationale: Thin new Infectum-wa cell; one context contrasts inability to apply officially with actual private applications.

summary: New sense 1: apply to an authority, approach an authority with a request

data.gloss: apply to an authority, approach an authority with a request

rationale: Makes explicit the application meaning already stated in the headword and exemplified by consulate/state appeals; formal access to the king is the same administrative sense.

data.translation: - Bei dem König sprachen sie gar nicht erst vor. -

rationale: Thin II Infectum cell; authority as fronted topic resumed by the object suffix.

data.turoyo: Afandəm u Brahim ġalabe naqqat mraǧaʕle d howe mabʕuṯ lə qadər.
data.translation: Sir, Brahim applied many times to become a ‘mabʕuṯ’ [member of parliament]; he could not.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell has three; explicit application purpose with authority omitted.

data.turoyo: W mraǧaʕli, kəllən am məketəbayḏe gabi, am məraǧaʕat dəṯṯe kəbʕət uʕdo gəd maḥwenoxne...
data.translation: And I made an application. I have all his letters with me, his correspondence. If you want, now I will show them to you...

rationale: Brings Preterit cell to five; first-person application supported by correspondence.

summary: Separate the personal-communication reference from the Turoyo text.
rationale: The final parenthesis is a source attribution, not Turoyo. The adjacent examples consistently store the same attribution in refs.

summary: The inherited II examples already support application to a consulate or state for a visa or assistance and the MAC permission request. The explicit numbered sense fills a structural gap rather than discovering a new meaning.
87/63 extends the same institutional approach to the king, with a fronted authority and a resumed -le. The negative clause does not require a separate consult sense.

arǧaʕ at PrS 6/34 is a return command inside a sultan's letter. Its meaning is clear from goal bayn ab Bani Halaliye, but code switching versus an integrated lexical loan is not settled by one imperative.
The existing etymology explicitly treats II as a contact-derived administrative denominative; that account is preserved, not replaced merely because an Arabic root-related return form appears.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English quotations below retain the supplied project machine translation and are marked as such; sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Where available, round-1 proposals are retained in the human layout and counts, and are not resubmitted in this JSON.
The empty original sense list was already repaired by round-1 II.1; no second structural correction or new apply sense is submitted.
Infectum-wa covers negated habitual applications and inability under latwoban. Bare mraǧaʕle remains Preterit despite ġalabe naqqat repeated occasions; frequency alone does not change its box.
The supplied contact-etymology discussion is preserved. Jan gives no new evidence deciding the status of the unrelated round-1 Arabic return command.
Is PrS 6/34 arǧaʕ integrated in Turoyo, and if so does it belong to the same entry as administrative II or to a separate homonym? Obtain attested base forms before creating a native I paradigm.
Confirm whether haw in 87/63 is straightforward negation and whether mraǧʕile is a 3pl Infectum with a 3sg authority object; the administrative sense itself is clear.
At 1.37/1550 is omitted-authority mraǧaʕwo a formal legal appeal, an administrative application or an informal petition? The general apply/approach sense is retained pending a procedural distinction.

Jan confirms the round-1 administrative application meaning for endowments/property and candidacy, with institutional targets omitted where recoverable. Official/private contrast concerns manner and access, not separate senses.
